description_full: MONY Group plc, together with its subsidiaries, provides price comparison and lead generation services through its websites and applications in the United Kingdom. The company operates through Insurance, Money, Home Services, Travel, and Cashback segments. It offers MoneySuperMarket, a price comparison site, which provides online and app-based tools to help people save money on their household bills; MoneySavingExpert, a consumer finance website; Quidco, a cashback site; TravelSupermarket for comparing prices on a range of holiday options, including package holidays and hotels, low-cost and charter airlines, and car hire providers; icelolly.com, a holiday price comparison website and deals platform; and Decision Tech, a B2B solution offers industry-leading comparison technology for third party brands. The company was formerly known as Moneysupermarket.com Group PLC and changed its name to MONY Group plc in May 2024. MONY Group plc was founded in 1993 and is based in Chester, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: MONY Group plc is a small-cap communication services business with a $1.3B market cap on $596M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 31% against a 7% cost of capital — a 24-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 67% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $131M in free cash flow — roughly 22 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.33× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.1× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 34× is fortress-like.
Management returns a meaningful 10.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation.

sect: Its 26% operating margin runs 17pp above the Communication Services median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.28x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 21% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 45% and a beta of 0.20, it is more defensive than the market.
Trading is thin (about $999 a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 0% in the 2020 crash and 0% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 40% below its DCF fair value of $16.67, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 20%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $12.16 to $24.12 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 10.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 11.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 9.4% annual cash-flow growth, 12pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 31% clears the cost of capital of 7.0% by 24pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.11).
It runs a 67% gross margin and converts 22% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.33x.
ROE of 36% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.7x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.1x net debt to EBITDA ($27.1M of cash against $45.4M of debt), with interest covered 33.5x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.9, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 54% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 7.1% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: It returns 10.0% a year to shareholders (3.1% in buybacks and 6.9% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years.
people: With about 629 employees, each generates about $948K of revenue, 1.6x the Communication Services median.
That works out to $208K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.9M (2x revenue per employee).
